result:
I reviewed the PR (three files: `claude_headless_adapter.py`, `flatline-orchestrator.sh`, `construct-index-gen.sh`) and wrote findings to `review.md`.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** (1 high, 3 medium/observations).

Key finding: removing the `OSError`/`ValueError` handlers around the `claude -p` subprocess spawn (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/claude_headless_adapter.py:151-182`) lets those exceptions propagate uncaught past the fallback-chain boundary — while the same file's `health_check()` (line 262) still treats `OSError` as an expected failure for the identical CLI call, confirming it's a real, not speculative, failure mode. That would crash the whole cheval run instead of letting flatline fall back to the next model.

The two shell-script changes (skeptic envelope normalization removal, and the construct-index-gen.sh revert to manifest-only field extraction) are flagged as medium-confidence observations — plausible intentional simplifications per the PR description, but each silently changes behavior for inputs I can't fully rule out given the frozen diff (no access to the scoring engine or actual pack manifests).
